notes.note: Glosses 'he see (after lam)' and 'you see (after lam, to a man)' read as broken English and differ from the house style 'he sees (form after 'lam')' used on day 41. Meaning is right.
يَرَى after أَنْ is glossed 'he sees' without '(after an)', unlike every other verb after an in the chunk. The form is correct (subjunctive = yarā); a learner might think the -a rule failed.
تَعْبَان is widely used but leans colloquial; the course itself uses MSA مُتْعَب from day 45. Consider مُتْعَبًا (after kuntu) for consistency.

After 38 / 37 the counted noun is accusative singular (دَرَجَةً). The bare دَرَجَة is accepted as a pause form under the house style, but these lines teach counting with numbers above 10, so the -an could be shown.
'put sa- (sa-) in front' is still doubled in the transliteration line (cosmetic; noted in round 2).
امْتِحَان (day 48) vs اِمْتِحَان with a kasra on the waṣl alif (day 50). Both are read the same, but the spelling convention differs.

summary: I read all 2,732 lines of days 41-50: 512 Arabic strings with a ⟶ line (sentences, mistake cards, dialogues, readings, quiz items, prose), about 2,100 seg glosses in context, and all 302 tap lines (620 tap glosses), and opened the sources where needed. The round-1/2 fixes have held. لَا and مَا now show the multi-sense glosses, يَحْضُرُ is present, and the form glosses for اِلْعَبِي and تَنَفَّسُوا are acceptable. I re-checked the grammar and found it all correct: lam + jussive (including lam tarudda, lam arahu, lam yara, -i before al-), an + subjunctive (ashtariya, an tashrabī without -na), imperatives and prohibitions (ibqa, irtaḥ, khudh, kul, nam, lā tansa/tansay, lā tansaw, ilʿabā), faʿlān feminines, body-part gender, number-noun agreement (thamānin/sabʿ wa-thalāthūna daraja, thalātha marrāt, miʾa wa-ʿishrūna junayhan, khamsa daqāʾiq), verb-subject order in the Juha story, and every quiz answer key. Arabic strings wrong: 0. Tap glosses wrong: 1 of 620 (مَرَّةً='times' on day 45 objectives, still unfixed from round 2). Errors: 5, all minor (1 gloss, 4 engine). The engine issues: empty brackets where a letter used to be doubled (a regression, 3 quiz prompts); inconsistent hyphenation of wa-/li-/fa- in about 15 words, against the round-3 clitic rule; a dropped -u on Allāhu mid-phrase; and the name Karīm in lower case. I found no major errors.
